answer: Proof of space-time curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to reserve physical storage indexed in a shared consensus atlas. During its operational voyage, an agent must answer challenges against stored plot files, yielding a violet cryptographic proof. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of purchasing dedicated disk drives and expending ongoing I/O bandwidth per identity. A key limitation is that datacenters with idle disk capacity can launch Sybils at negligible marginal cost.
